condition: Two-step route, observed Claude/Cowork mode labels, visible folder-ready check, exact save location and OS-specific opening.
scope: Ten synthetic personas × three independent HTML reads for each version. Each used the same question, model and OS assignments. Readers assumed access to Cowork and the demonstrations described in captions.
question:
Claude Desktop is already installed and your account has Cowork access. No course folder or previous course conversation exists. There is no trainer. You are trying this on your own.

Below is actual HTML from the handbook: navigation, cover, Start, contents and Prework, in their actual order. Cowork is selected; other runtime content is hidden and omitted. Initially closed panels show only their labels; their contents are available when opened. The Mac/Windows control starts on your computer's OS and can switch the setup directions. The rest of the handbook, including linked reading destinations, exists beyond this excerpt. Assess the start, not omitted later material. This is an HTML-reading simulation, not actual app execution or a visual screenshot test.

Based only on the HTML, describe what you would do, in order, until you could open and try the first game. Would you get going? How quick and obvious would that route feel to you? Report any hesitation, detour, need for help or reason to stop; if there is none, say so. Do not invent app behaviour or claim you executed anything.

Give a rating from 1.0 to 5.0 stars, in steps of 0.1. Keep these anchors: 1.0=cannot get going; 2.0=need substantial help; 3.0=can get going with detours; 4.0=clear with minor hesitation; 5.0=snappy and obvious throughout. Use values between anchors when they fit your experience better. Rate the route to the first visible result (the game), not full Prework completion or course quality. Report predicted getting going separately from smoothness.

Quote the instruction most relevant to your rating. Name the one change that would help you most, if any; none is allowed. Under 250 words. Return JSON with stars (number from 1.0 to 5.0 in steps of 0.1), wouldGetGoing (yes, no, or uncertain), firstActions (array), hesitations (array; empty if none), evidenceQuote (exact instruction text), feeling (your own voice), biggestImprovement (text; none if no change needed).

Where the HTML says to assume a video is here, assume the described demonstration is available. Do not invent content beyond its caption.

Observed native folder labels and follow-up permission, explicit ready state and activity handoff, file-opening recovery on demand.

Short primary route with an estimated few minutes, alternate app labels in help, explicit repeat permission after Send, and optional other tools.

limits: Persona scores measure perceived clarity through the first game. A separate native Mac run exercised the same prompt against an empty local folder and played the saved game in a browser. Elapsed time, human completion, Windows behavior and automatic course loading remain unmeasured.
